title: Competitors and market
hired_for: To show the owner what rivals are doing with price, offers, products and ads, and where there is room to win, so the brand stops losing buyers to them without knowing why.

jobs.job: Tell me when a rival cuts price or starts a sale that could take my sales
jobs.why: A rival's 30% off week can pull buyers away before the owner notices the dip. Knowing the same day lets them hold, match with a bundle or shift ad spend.

watch.metric: our price against tracked rivals on matched products, checked daily
watch.source: rival product pages captured into the brand brain, with Shopify prices

drives.metric: conversion rate on matched products, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a rival's 30% sitewide sale is found a week late, after conversion fell 15%. After: it is flagged the same day and a bundle offer holds conversion within 5%.
jobs.who_today: founder, by checking rival sites now and then

jobs.job: Check my price sits inside the range buyers expect for this category
jobs.why: Priced far above the range with no clear reason, buyers leave. Priced far below, the brand leaves margin behind and looks cheap.

watch.metric: our price per unit against the tracked rival range, same pack size, monthly
watch.source: rival product pages captured into the brand brain, with Shopify prices

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: our 6 pack is 35% above the top of the rival range with no reason on the page. After: the reason is added or the pack is resized, and gross profit per visitor rises 8%.

jobs.job: Stop discounting deeper than rivals while claiming to be premium
jobs.why: Deep, frequent discounts undo a premium price and train buyers to wait. If rivals discount less, we are giving away margin for nothing.

watch.metric: our average discount depth against tracked rivals, 30 days
watch.source: Shopify discounts and rival sale prices captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: we run 25% off 4 times a quarter while rivals run 15% twice. After: sales drop to 2 a quarter and gross margin rises 3 points.

jobs.job: Know when rivals change their shipping, returns or guarantee
jobs.why: Free returns or a longer guarantee from a rival can shift buyers fast. The owner needs to know to match it or explain why we are still better.

watch.metric: rival policy changes on shipping, returns and guarantees, weekly
watch.source: rival policy pages captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a rival moved to free returns and we find out from a support ticket. After: it is flagged in a day and our page answers it within a week.

jobs.job: See who is bidding on my brand name and core search terms
jobs.why: Rivals buying ads on our name take buyers who were already looking for us, and push up what we pay for our own name.

watch.metric: share of our brand name searches where our ad shows, and which rivals show, 7 days
watch.source: Google Ads auction insights

drives.metric: cost per click on brand name terms

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 2 rivals show on 40% of our brand name searches. After: our ad shows on 95% of them and brand clicks cost 20% less.

jobs.job: Give support a true, checked answer to 'how are you different from them'
jobs.why: When a shopper asks in chat and gets a vague reply, the sale is lost. A checked answer per rival wins it.

watch.metric: conversion rate on chats that mention a rival, 30 days
watch.source: Gorgias chats linked to Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 20% of chats that name a rival end in a sale. After: a checked answer per rival lifts it to 32%.

jobs.job: Know when a rival launches a new product or starts selling in a new place
jobs.why: A rival's new product or move onto Amazon or into a big retailer can take buyers in weeks. Early warning gives time to respond.

watch.metric: new rival products and new sales channels spotted, weekly
watch.source: rival sites, Amazon and retailer listings captured into the brand brain

drives.metric: our revenue in the matched product line

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a rival's new wool line is spotted 2 months after launch. After: it is flagged in week 1 and our wool page is refreshed before the cold season.

jobs.job: Read rival reviews for complaints we can fix and win on
jobs.why: Rival buyers say in reviews what they wish was better. If we fix that and say so, we win them.

watch.metric: share of rival 1 to 3 star reviews by theme, quarter
watch.source: public reviews on Amazon and rival sites, stored in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 28% of a rival's bad reviews say holes after 3 months, and our page does not mention durability. After: a durability promise goes on our page and conversion rises 10%.

jobs.job: Know which weeks rivals run big sales, and plan around them
jobs.why: When rivals run sitewide sales, our conversion drops. Knowing their calendar lets the owner plan offers and ad spend, not react.

watch.metric: our conversion rate in weeks rivals run sitewide sales against other weeks
watch.source: Shopify and GA4, with rival sale dates captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: conversion drops 20% in rival sale weeks with no plan. After: a bundle and lower spend on new-buyer ads hold the drop to 8%.

jobs.job: Compare rival pages and offers for what we lack
jobs.why: A rival's bundle, trial or size guide can win buyers we lose. A side-by-side view shows what is worth adding.

watch.metric: offer features rivals have that we do not, per matched product
watch.source: rival product pages captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 5 of 7 rivals offer a mix and match 3 pack and we do not. After: it is added and units per order rise 12%.

jobs.job: Spot a rival that is weak right now so we can win their buyers
jobs.why: A rival that runs out of stock or pulls back ads leaves buyers searching. Those buyers are cheap to win for a short time.

watch.metric: rival out-of-stock days on matched products and rival ad count drops, weekly
watch.source: rival product pages and Meta Ad Library, captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a rival's best seller is out for 3 weeks and nobody notices. After: we raise spend on that search term in week 1 and add 400 new customers.

jobs.job: Know which rival moves matter and skip the noise
jobs.why: Rivals change something every day. The owner wants only the changes that could cost sales, not a feed of everything.

watch.metric: rival alerts per week that led to an action (a proxy for signal over noise)
watch.source: alert log in the brand brain

drives.metric: hours the owner spends on rival watching per week

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 60 rival changes a week, 2 matter. After: 4 alerts a week, 3 lead to action.

jobs.job: Test my positioning against a rival's before I spend on it
jobs.why: A position that sounds good in a meeting can lose to a rival's in the feed. A small test tells the owner which one buyers pick.

watch.metric: click-through rate and cost per purchase for 2 positioning angles, 14 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the brand bets its fall campaign on 'most comfortable'. After: a $1,500 test shows 'lasts 2 times longer' wins at 30% lower cost per purchase.

jobs.job: Learn why almost-buyers chose a named rival instead of us
jobs.why: Every lost sale has a reason. If the same reason keeps coming up, fixing it wins back a steady stream of buyers.

watch.metric: lost-sale reasons that name a rival, quarter (survey and chat answers are a proxy)
watch.source: exit survey answers and Gorgias chats

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: nobody knows why buyers leave. After: 40% of named losses say the rival had a 30 day trial, and a trial test starts next month.

jobs.job: Catch a search term or product type growing faster than my category
jobs.why: Buyers can move to a cheaper swap or a new format. If that shift is spotted early, the brand can move with them.

watch.metric: search demand growth for substitute terms against our category terms, quarter
watch.source: Google Trends and Google Ads Keyword Planner, stored in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 'compression socks' searches grow 3 times faster than ours and we have none. After: the shift is flagged and a test product is in sampling next quarter.

jobs.job: Read rival ads for new angles, as signals and not as proof
jobs.why: Rival ads that run for months hint at what works for them. The owner wants the angles, not a copy of their ads.

watch.metric: new rival ad angles running 30 days or more, weekly
watch.source: Meta Ad Library, captured into the brand brain

drives.metric: share of our new ad tests that beat the account median

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the team scrolls the ad library for an hour a week. After: 3 new long-running angles are listed each Monday, and 1 feeds our next test.

jobs.job: See how we rank against rivals on Amazon for our core search terms
jobs.why: On Amazon, the top few results take most of the clicks. Slipping from the first page means lost sales we never see.

watch.metric: our share of the top 10 results on core Amazon search terms, weekly
watch.source: Amazon Brand Analytics and marketplace seller tools

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: we hold 1 of the top 10 slots on 'athletic socks'. After: 3 slots within a quarter after listing and review fixes.

jobs.job: Map every real alternative a shopper weighs, including doing nothing
jobs.why: The real rival might be a 10 pack from a big store or just old socks in the drawer. If the owner fights the wrong rival, the message misses.

watch.metric: real alternatives mapped, with the reason buyers pick each
watch.source: brand brain, built from reviews, surveys and search terms

drives.metric: click-through rate on ads that name the real alternative

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the brand compares itself only to 2 online-only rivals. After: 'cheap multi-pack' is named as the main rival and a cost-per-wear ad wins.

jobs.job: Know when a rival copies our product, claim or photos
jobs.why: Copies confuse buyers and can take sales on our own name. Some need a takedown request, some need a new claim.

watch.metric: rival pages or ads found using our claims or images
watch.source: rival pages and Meta Ad Library, captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a rival uses our product photo in ads for a month. After: it is found in a week and a takedown is filed.

jobs.job: Find open space in the market that no rival claims
jobs.why: Fighting the leader head-on is costly. A need or angle nobody owns can be won for far less.

watch.metric: unclaimed angles with real search demand, mapped each quarter
watch.source: positioning map in the brand brain, with Google Ads Keyword Planner demand

drives.metric: cost per new customer on ads built for the open angle

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: every rival says 'comfort'. After: 'made for 12 hour shifts' shows real demand and no rival claims it, and a test ad set runs at 25% lower cost.

jobs.job: See which rivals are growing fastest
jobs.why: Fast-growing rivals are the ones to learn from and the ones that will take share next.

watch.metric: rival review count growth per month and active ad count, monthly (proxies for sales growth)
watch.source: Amazon and rival review counts and Meta Ad Library, captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a rival that tripled its reviews in 6 months is not on the watch list. After: it is added and its lead offer is studied.

jobs.job: See our share of rival ad activity
jobs.why: If rivals run 10 times our ads, they will be seen more. It is a rough signal of who is pushing hardest right now.

watch.metric: our active ads as a share of all tracked brands' active ads, weekly (a public signal, not spend)
watch.source: Meta Ad Library, captured into the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: we run 12 ads, the top rival runs 140. After: the gap is known and our test volume doubles.

jobs.job: Compare how premium we look against rivals
jobs.why: Packaging, photos, proof and guarantees tell buyers what price is fair before they read the price. If we look cheaper than we cost, buyers leave.

watch.metric: premium signals on our page against the rival average
watch.source: page check in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: rivals show 6 premium signals, we show 3. After: we add 3 and full-price conversion rises 7%.

jobs.job: Size my market and a new niche from my own numbers
jobs.why: A niche that looks big online may not hold enough buyers at our price. Sizing it from our own order value and repeat rate tells the owner if it can carry the business.

watch.metric: buyers needed per year at our order value and margin, against estimated niche demand
watch.source: Shopify orders with Google Ads Keyword Planner demand

drives.metric: revenue from the niche, first year

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a niche is chosen because it feels big. After: the math shows it needs 40,000 buyers a year and has about 15,000, so the brand picks a broader one.
